method: Use production full host packets and production dateReviewJobs/retainedDateReviewJobs/dateWorkerInput. Clone final independent-review inputs in memory, delete only units[*].en and units[*].literal if present, assert exact equality of every other field. Do not write projected payloads, host plans, states, inputs, hashes or approvals.
limits: Byte savings do not establish token savings, quality or approved-chapter throughput. Never rewrite existing sealed plans, claims, source/extraction fingerprints or approvals.

recommendation.verdict: Recommend a versioned Chinese-only source-unit view for genuinely fresh independent-review jobs after host review; preserve retained bilingual jobs unchanged.
seam: Keep buildDateAuditPacket and its complete sourceHash/extractionHash calculation unchanged.

Persist an explicit source-view version in newly sealed review plans before any dispatch; absence means current legacy view. Never retrofit a retained plan, retained conversation or accepted artifact.

Bind the view version and resulting payload hash into fresh job identity/provenance. Retained job IDs, packet ownership, byte ceilings, split plans, sticky inputs, and independence/publication gates remain unchanged.

Apply the chosen projection through the shared independent-review dateWorkerInput path for every lane, only under its persisted fresh-plan version. Keep English people/claim/context-item values, instructions, source URLs, every locator and all Chinese evidence unchanged.
Keep current planning ownership and ceilings for initial rollout; do not use projected byte savings to enlarge jobs or weaken coverage. Require production validators and independent review as before.
Do not claim the existing re-audit2 conversations are Chinese-only; they have already seen English. No paid calibration or dispatch was performed.
risks: A blank-Chinese unit with useful English-only metadata would lose that context; inspect and explicitly handle such inputs rather than silently hiding missing Chinese evidence.

Current unit metadata retains only id and blockIndex in addition to zh/en: table kind/collection/header relationships are not newly supplied by this projection. English table labels can encode inferred dates; removing them does not reconstruct missing Chinese heading context.
English source text can contain editorial notes, disambiguations or bibliographic metadata absent from zh. Those may need a separately labeled non-evidence channel if supported by a concrete case.
English chronology remains in claims and hints under review; this experiment does not make the whole prompt linguistically independent of prior extraction.
The host source fingerprint should still invalidate work when either Chinese or English source fields change; retaining that behavior is intentional.
